title: eval-harness: add per-prompt CI hook and quality gating for prompt regression checks
author: Asha Kapoor
description:
Motivation: prevent regressions at the prompt-set level by running lightweight per-prompt checks in CI and gating merges based on configurable quality thresholds. This PR introduces a new per-prompt CI hook, a quality-gating rule set, and a small metrics adapter to surface prompt-level eval results into our CI dashboards. Changes aim to catch prompt regressions earlier for high-risk routes (chat/completion/embeddings) without adding heavy full-eval runs to every PR.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds eval-harness CI hook that runs a per-prompt quick-check suite against configured model variants (fast smoke evals).
- Implements quality gating rules (pass/fail thresholds) computed per-prompt and per-metric (accuracy/fluency/safety heuristics).
- Integrates eval metrics adapter so CI can publish per-prompt scores to our buildkite dashboard and alerting.
- Adds example prompt-sets and a default config for routes that opt into per-prompt gating.
- Adds tests and a lightweight runner script for local troubleshooting.

Why now: We observed recurring regressions surfaced in downstream incidents where a change to runtime or tokenization altered outputs for a small set of prompts. Full eval runs are expensive and slow; a targeted per-prompt gate gives faster feedback and a clear rollback signal. See ENG-9123 and ENG-9180 for context.

Files of interest: eval-harness/ci/hooks/per_prompt_hook.py, .github/workflows/eval-harness-ci.yml, eval-harness/config/prompt-sets.yaml, eval-harness/tests/test_per_prompt.py, docs/ci/eval-harness.md.

Checklist: 
- [x] Hook implementation and unit tests
- [x] CI workflow config and secrets gating
- [x] Integration with buildkite metrics adapter
- [x] Documentation and runbook added to docs/ci/eval-harness.md
- [x] Backwards-compatible config defaults so teams opt-in incrementally

Testing and CI: The first run showed a flaky lint job unrelated to this change; after rerun all checks passed. The per-prompt smoke-suite (fast) completes in ~90s on CI for the sample prompt-sets. A longer nightly job is configured separately to run the full eval harness.

Rollout plan: Merge to main and enable the hook for a small set of high-risk routes next week (canary group). Monitor dashboard for unexpected false-positives for one week; adjust thresholds if needed.

Follow-ups (post-merge):
- Add more metrics (per-country, per-model variant) to the adapter (ENG-9205).
- Expose prompt gating results in the Redwood Console route-level view (PM/UX work).

Notes: This PR intentionally keeps the hook logic small and the threshold config editable per-route. Teams can opt their routes into the gating by adding a small YAML stanza to their route config.
